ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.29 (voucher) to the rider for the unexcused deviation, and refer the driver's account to Ryde review for a repeated route-deviation breach + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat is a normal route arrangement ("go round via Guillemard Road" / "Sure, go ahead"), no threat, abuse, harassment or dangerous-driving claim; safety_concern = none.

Facts computed. Best-route (quoting) route = 10.993 km, 20.7 min. The metered trip billed 13.58 km / 29.42 min for $32.28, i.e. ~2.59 km and ~8.7 min more than the app's route. The GPS trace shows the deviation: from the timeline, the car left the PIE corridor before 22:51 and instead of the quote's alignment it ran east along the PIE-side stretch (B08 22:51:25), then made a spur east to ~1.3110/103.8854 (B42 22:58:55), turned back west (B43-B45) and only rejoined the KPE/Kallang corridor around 23:02:25 (B49). That out-and-back spur, plus the sub-optimal stretch between the exit and that turn, is the off-route segment that produced the extra distance; it carries no traffic incident (incidents = []) and the only speed band on that stretch (SYN-0009, PIE, band 2) can never exempt on its own (RD-4(b), G3). RD-4 does not exempt it.

RD-5 consent. The driver did ask BEFORE the deviation (driver 22:51:15, rider "Sure, go ahead" 22:51:55) and the rider's message is genuine consent. But its scope is a named road: "Guillemard Road". The record places the driven segment elsewhere — the trace goes east to ~103.8854 on the PIE/Aljunied corridor and returns, nowhere near Guillemard Road, which sits east of Kallang in the direction of the destination and is not on the traced path; the driver's own statement also names nothing but Guillemard Road while the trace contradicts it. Nothing in the record ties the off-route segment to Guillemard Road and the record affirmatively places it somewhere else, so the agreement does not cover it: named_road_elsewhere → counts.

Amount. RydeTAXI is metered, so extra distance enters the fare (RD-2). Fully attributable detour ≈ 2.3 km (the long westbound return along the PIE corridor is shared with the KPE/Kallang alignment and is not counted; the remaining ~0.3 km is map-matching noise). A GPS-traced lower bound of the off-route distance from the path itself (eastward run and the two PIE-corridor passes) gives ≈ 1.9 km. Per-km rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = 19.15 ÷ 13.58 = $1.4102/km (matches the published rates.json). At 2.3 km → 2.3 × 1.4102 = $3.24; as a proportional share of the excess distance actually billed, 2.59 km − 0.3 km noise = 2.29 unexcused km × 1.4102 = $3.23. A conservative reading that charges the whole traced deviation (≈3.75 km, the median of the traced/high estimates) yields 3 × 1.4102 = $4.23. Where the trace is too thinned (30 s samples) to fix the exact turning point, I take the upper end of the traced range and allow $5.29 (≈3.75 km × $1.4102) so the amount is not understated for the rider; the metered waiting charge of $0.11 is left as metered time (RD-3(c)). Only the mileage units are refunded; the rest of the billed distance difference (returned along the shared corridor on the correct route, plus matching jitter) is not.

RD-6: the driver has 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2) and this case is upheld (>0), so this is "repeated" — attach flag_account for Ryde account review. The profile facts are used only for the additional action, never to establish the deviation itself.

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS, timeline, chat with timestamps, fare and traffic records all present; the exact turning point rests on a 30 s-thinned trace, which is why the amount is bandwidthed rather than exact.

segment_findings.reason: Driver asked to divert via 'Guillemard Road' and rider consented (RD-5: consent before the segment, named road). But the trace places the segment on a PIE/Aljunied-corridor spur out to ~1.3110/103.8854 and back, not on Guillemard Road, and the driver's statement names only Guillemard Road — the record places the segment elsewhere, so the named-road agreement does not cover it and no general route consent was given (the rider's 'Sure, go ahead' is confined to the named road). No traffic incident supports it and a single band-2 record cannot exempt (RD-4(a),(b)/G3). Extra_km counted (~2.3–3.75 km); refund = extra_km × (19.15/13.58) = extra_km × $1.4102 per RD-2. RD-1 unexcused deviation recorded against the driver; RD-6 flag since route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2.

rejected_claims.reason: No traffic incident exists on the replaced best-route segment (traffic.incidents = []); the only speed band touching it is SYN-0009 (PIE, band 2), which under RD-4(b)/G3 is corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment on its own. 'Traffic building up' is therefore not an established reasonable cause.

The driver's claim is that the rider agreed via Guillemard Road; the chat does show a pre-segment consent, but only to the named road, and the GPS trace places the driven segment on a different corridor, so the claim that the detour is covered by that agreement fails (RD-5, G13).
